blocks.text: Ezekiel 24 reports the death of the prophet's wife, whom Ezekiel calls 'the delight of his eyes'—language expressing intimate attachment. The event is presented as a sign to the household of Israel concerning the sanctuary and bereavement. Notably, Ezekiel is forbidden to perform customary mourning rituals. This restriction transforms private loss into public prophecy; the prophet's constrained grief becomes instruction to Israel about enduring unbearable loss without the comfort of traditional mourning practices.
